page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-48 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance within the n4a server family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Operating on the arm64 architecture, this server type is designed for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from high-density multi-core processing. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution performance without resource contention. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture combined with a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio offers a resource-dense profile for parallel processing tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage.

The n4a-highcpu-48 is suited for multi-threaded compute workloads, such as containerized microservices, web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and distributed analytics. Because it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O or hardware-accelerated graphics and machine learning training must rely on external network-attached storage and CPU-based execution.
